input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision (no change-of-control language appears anywhere, and Sections 13/14 create no transfer-triggered rights). It fails the fallback on material terms: there is no successor carve-out at all, so a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets of Client requires TrueLink's approval; there is no reasonableness standard on that approval; and the retained no-consent affiliate exception (which also runs in TrueLink's favour) is inconsistent with the fallback requirement that other assignments require consent. We therefore target the preferred position: Client may assign without approval to an affiliate or to a successor in an M&A or asset sale, TrueLink may assign only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor of ours, and a change of control of Client gives TrueLink no termination right.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of Client, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, and shall never assign to a competitor of Client.

ops.text: Client may assign or transfer its rights under this Agreement without approval to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and a change of control of Client shall give TrueLink no right to terminate this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We recast Section 15 so only TrueLink needs our consent to assign (not to be unreasonably withheld, and never to a competitor of ours), and we added our consent-free right to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets together with confirmation that a change of control of Client gives TrueLink no termination right. If preferred, we can fall back to a mutual successor right on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
proposal.summary: Limit the assignment consent requirement to TrueLink (consent not unreasonably withheld, never to a Client competitor) and add Client's consent-free affiliate/successor assignment right plus no TrueLink termination right on Client's change of control.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
